themes.title: Transnational Right Weaponizes French Riots and Unrest
themes.blurb: Right-wing media and political strategists in France and the United States are seizing on recent urban violence in France to reinforce strict law-and-order platforms. While Marine Le Pen frames the unrest as proof of a collapsing state, American conservative media and Trump campaign figures leverage the events as a cautionary narrative to rally their base.

countries.name: 🇫🇷 Rassemblement National
countries.note: Marine Le Pen uses recent riots to declare the French state is collapsing and position her party as the sole restorer of order.

countries.name: 🇺🇸 MAGA / Trump
countries.note: Trump campaign strategists exploit French urban violence to energize conservative voters ahead of U.S. midterms.

themes.title: Hardline Anti-Immigration Policies and Border Enforcement Surge
themes.blurb: Populist right parties in Europe and North America are simultaneously pushing aggressive measures to restrict immigration and tighten border controls. Proposals range from externalizing asylum processing to third countries in Norway to purging noncitizen voter rolls and ramping up deportation crackdowns in the U.S.

countries.name: 🇳🇴 Fremskrittspartiet
countries.note: Sylvi Listhaug proposes restricting family reunification, limiting permanent residency, and moving asylum processing to third countries.

countries.name: 🇺🇸 MAGA / Trump
countries.note: The Trump administration pursues voter roll purges, aggressive ICE enforcement tactics, and hardline border rhetoric.

themes.title: Populist Right Gains Momentum Amid Incumbent Vulnerabilities
themes.blurb: Right-wing populist parties across multiple Western democracies are capitalizing on the declining popularity of incumbent center and left leaders. Strong polling numbers and energized rally turnout are strengthening right-wing momentum ahead of key legislative and executive elections.

countries.name: 🇫🇷 Rassemblement National

countries.name: 🇺🇸 MAGA / Trump

themes.blurb: Right-wing parties in Sweden, the US, and France face public scrutiny and voter pushback resulting from internal strife, divisive rhetoric, and local administrative failures. These friction points threaten to complicate broader political momentum.
